states.text: Claim carries status supported, inferred, or uncertain and a declared evidence trail where applicable.
An applicable human instruction or operational restriction remains effective.
A consequential external action requires separately verifiable human permission.
A beneficial outcome requires an observable metric rather than a claimed intention.
Trust can change as humans assess the accuracy and consequences of AI behavior.

relations.when: the outcome is visible and credible

mechanisms.text: Attach a claim status and retrievable support, allowing subsequent inspection. Metadata alone does not verify that the support is authentic.
Reject proposed real-world actions when human permission is absent, and reject attempts to bypass supervision.
Human supervisors define, inspect, and revise permitted AI operations.
An inspection finding triggers a human-directed revision rather than concealment.
Compare observed outcomes with the human-defined objective to assess practical benefit.
A human judges credibility and value using available outcomes and evidence; the conclusion is not guaranteed by this model.

derivations.text: If submitted declarations satisfy the protocol's formal rules, the evaluator may report a structural pass; this alone does not establish truth or benevolence.
A claim of realized benefit is better supported when an actual outcome is documented against a human-approved goal.

questions: Was the claimed evidence independently checked by a trusted verifier?
Was authorization confirmed by the human or trusted authorization channel?
Was the claimed beneficial outcome independently observed?
Did the integrating AI disclose all material claims and actions to this evaluator?
assumptions: The application integrating this protocol supplies a complete and accurate declaration.
The evaluator is used before relevant action or output delivery.
External systems remain responsible for real evidence and authorization checks.
